problems.reason: All four sentences state the same fact that the genus Knoetschkesuchus contains two species, K. langenbergensis and K. guimarotae, and that the latter was originally named Theriosuchus guimarotae.
Both sentences describe the diet of Knoetschkesuchus as primarily invertebrates and possibly small vertebrates.
Sentence 22 repeats the information that both species were formerly classified in Theriosuchus, already stated in earlier sentences.
Sentence 28 discusses the geological setting of Europe during the Kimmeridgian, which is unrelated to the biology of Knoetschkesuchus.
Sentences 29 and 30 describe the geological basins and massifs where the fossils were found, not characteristics of the animal itself.
